goal: Create crates/monokl/src/types.rs (SymbolKind, Visibility, SymbolEntry) and crates/monokl/src/tests_types.rs (their serde-contract test suite) from scratch, per SPEC-003 -- both module files lib.rs already declares (pub mod types; #[cfg(test)] mod tests_types;) but which do not yet exist on disk.
architecture: types.rs is built incrementally in AC-001's declared order -- SymbolKind first, then Visibility, then SymbolEntry, since SymbolEntry's fields reference the other two as types -- with every structural task (T-001, T-003, T-006) performing a full-file overwrite of the complete cumulative content so the file is always syntactically well-formed (balanced braces) at every commit, verified purely by diff/grep against exact expected content (no cargo invocation, matching PLAN-004's established pattern for this workspace's io-errors/orin-cargo registry blocker). tests_types.rs is built alongside it, one behavioral acceptance criterion per task, each full-file overwrite verified two ways: diff/grep against the real committed file, and a real `cargo test` run inside an isolated /tmp fixture crate (serde+serde_json only, no io-errors dependency) that mirrors this project's exact src/lib.rs + src/types.rs + src/tests_types.rs module layout -- the same isolation technique PLAN-001 established for error.rs. Every fixture command and every expected error string or pass-count quoted in this plan's steps was captured from a real `cargo test` run against this exact content during planning, not guessed. Revised after vector-challenger review: (1) T-003's Visibility variant-count grep is now scoped strictly to the Visibility enum's own body via an awk line-range, since a whole-file grep alternation also matched SymbolKind's own Module variant; (2) T-006's impl_owner-mentions grep is now anchored to a single specific doc-comment line, since the prior whole-file grep counted a 4-line doc-comment discussion as 4 separate matches; (3) T-007 now includes a real serialize/deserialize test proving traitImpl/kindDetail camelCase renaming (AC-004) actually takes effect; (4) T-008's extra-key test now proves the unrecognized impl_owner key is truly ignored rather than aliased onto owner (AC-006/AC-007); (5) T-010's explicit-null test now covers all 5 Option-typed fields, not 2 (AC-010); (6) T-009's missing-field test now asserts the error message names the specific missing field (AC-011); (7) fixture Cargo.toml files now pin edition = "2024" with a [lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny" table, matching this workspace's real edition/lints instead of edition 2021 with no lint table, so a green fixture result is a stronger proxy for the real crate; (8) see shared_file_warning below for the types.rs clobbering-risk note. Every fixture command and expected output in this revision was independently re-run for real during this review pass -- including deliberately mutating the fixture the way vector-challenger did (deleting rename_all, aliasing impl_owner onto owner) to confirm the strengthened tests actually catch those regressions -- not re-assumed from the prior draft.
shared_file_warning: crates/monokl/src/types.rs is a SHARED file. This plan (SPEC-003) creates it from scratch across T-001, T-003, and T-006 using full-file overwrites (`cat > types.rs <<EOF`) verified by whole-file diff -- this is safe here because each overwrite supplies the complete, correct cumulative content for everything this plan owns. SPEC-005, SPEC-006, SPEC-007, and SPEC-008's own plans will each need to add further type definitions to this same file. Any future plan targeting types.rs after this plan has run MUST NOT perform a blind full-file overwrite -- doing so would silently clobber SymbolKind/Visibility/SymbolEntry (or whatever an intervening plan added). Future plans must use append-based or precisely-scoped edits (e.g., appending a new type definition after the file's last `}`, verified with a scoped grep/awk check rather than a whole-file diff) once this plan's content already exists on disk. This plan cannot enforce that on plans it does not control -- this note exists to reduce, not eliminate, the risk of a future plan silently clobbering this one's work. See also T-006's shared_file_note and T-011's final step, where this warning is repeated at the point of last contact with types.rs and tests_types.rs respectively.
reasoning:
Verified before writing this plan: crates/monokl/src/lib.rs (SPEC-004, already implemented) declares `pub mod types;` and, separately, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests_types;` -- neither crates/monokl/src/types.rs nor crates/monokl/src/tests_types.rs exists on disk yet (confirmed via `find`/`ls`); PLAN-004's own architecture note explicitly assigns creating those files to each module's own track, not PLAN-004's -- so this plan creates both. SPEC-003's own scope and non_goals confirm these three types have no dependency on MonoklError or the io-errors blocker (plain data types, no fallible construction) -- confirmed by reading api_surface: none of SymbolKind/Visibility/SymbolEntry's signatures reference crate::error, and non_goals never mentions error.rs. All 12 acceptance criteria (AC-001..AC-012) are covered with zero deferrals -- this spec carries no blocker analogous to SPEC-001's io-errors gap; its own scope statement confirms these are plain serde-derived data types. covers_criteria mapping: AC-001->T-001 (SymbolKind structural), AC-002->T-002 (SymbolKind camelCase behavior), AC-003->T-003+T-004 (Visibility structural + behavior), AC-008->T-003 (Visibility no-Super naming contract, co-located with the enum's own doc comment since that is where the contract is actually stated in code), AC-009->T-005 (unknown-variant rejection for both enums, tested together since the criterion covers both), AC-004->T-006 (SymbolEntry structural), AC-007->T-006 (owner naming contract, co-located with the field's own doc comment), AC-005->T-007 (serialize asymmetry + missing-key deserialize), AC-006->T-008 (extra key discarded), AC-011->T-009 (missing required field), AC-010->T-010 (explicit null), AC-012->T-011 (line bounds/type validation). Every fixture cargo invocation in this plan was actually run during planning against the exact cumulative file content each task writes (confirmed at three checkpoints: 4 tests after Visibility's camelCase+unknown-variant tests, and the full 12 tests against the final types.rs+tests_types.rs content laid out exactly as it will exist in the real crate), not assumed to work. AC-007/AC-008's judgment_call is honored by giving each defect's doc comment an exact, literal citation (line numbers, finding numbers) rather than paraphrasing, matching the spec's own conditional framing ('if written as literally specified there, would not compile') instead of asserting 04-analysis-fidelity.md's prose is itself broken.

Correction pass following vector-challenger's FAIL verdict (8 issues), each independently re-verified by actually running the commands and, where the issue concerned a missing behavioral test, actually mutating the fixture the way the reviewer described to confirm the new/strengthened test fails on the mutation and passes on the correct code: (1) T-003's Visibility grep re-scoped via awk range (verified: naive pattern returns 5, scoped pattern returns 4, against the real T-003 file content); (2) T-006's impl_owner grep re-anchored to one doc-comment line (verified: naive pattern returns 4, anchored pattern returns 1); (3) added trait_impl_kind_detail_camel_case_keys to T-007 for AC-004 (verified: fails with rename_all deleted, observed literal `"trait_impl":"Bar"` in the serialized output); (4) strengthened T-008's extra-key test to assert owner comes only from the correctly-named key (verified: fails with a duplicate-field error when owner carries #[serde(alias = "impl_owner")]); (5) extended T-010's explicit-null test from 2 to all 5 Option fields (verified against real serde_json: all five null keys deserialize to None); (6) strengthened T-009's missing-field test to assert the error names the specific field (verified real error strings: "missing field `name`"/`kind`/`line`, each at the exact byte offset serde_json reports for this struct); (7) added a top-level shared_file_warning plus matching notes on T-006 and T-011 about types.rs being a file SPEC-005 through SPEC-008 will also extend; (8) all fixture Cargo.toml blocks (T-002, T-004, T-005, T-007 through T-011) now pin edition = "2024" with a [lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny" table instead of edition 2021 with no lint table, matching the real workspace root Cargo.toml (edition.workspace = true = "2024", rust-version 1.96) and crates/monokl/Cargo.toml ([lints] workspace = true) -- confirmed by reading both files directly; local `rustc --version`/`cargo --version` both report 1.96.0, confirming edition 2024 fixtures actually build in this environment. The full 13-test final tests_types.rs content (T-011's cumulative state) was run end-to-end against a real cargo test invocation on an edition-2024 fixture with this lints table during this review and produced `test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed`, exit 0.
